correctness.rationale: For every \(q\ge2\), every four-coordinate word has one of exactly 15 restricted-growth equality patterns. Direct rational summation of the distinct one-deletion target weights never exceeds 1 (all 15 are displayed, tested by stdlib checker). A symbolic count of the q, \(2q(q-1)\), q(q-1), \(q(q-1)(q-2)\) distinct target-type multiplicities gives weight \(q(2q^2+q+1)/8\), a valid fractional packing dual. At q=4 the total is \(37/2\); the 19 explicitly listed quaternary words have distinct deletion descendants covering all 64 targets. Coverage check gives multiplicities {1:60,2:4}. Thus 19<=\(D\le19\); no heuristic or incomplete enumeration is used as proof. Boundaries q=2 and q=3 work, and all q use symbolic equality-pattern reduction.

evidence: Xie–Sun–Ge provide \(D(q,n,R)\ge q^{n-R}/\binom nR\), giving 16 when \(q=4,n=4,R=1\), and an asymptotic \(q\to\infty\) upper bound, not the exact value 19.

Lenz–Rashtchian–Siegel–Yaakobi Theorem 3 gives a distinct general weighted lower bound; at \(q=4,n=4,R=1\) the explicit theorem sum is 4(1/3+6/4+9/5)=218/15≈14.53, below the present \(37/2\) certificate.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither general published bound entails a 19-word minimum. The asymptotic statement allows subleading finite-alphabet effects and cannot imply the exact finite value. The present packing has total weight \(37/2\) and the explicit code proves attainability.

value.rationale: Minimum deletion-covering cardinality for short nonbinary blocks is a natural exact invariant motivated by the 2026 covering-code paper. The elementary counting lower bound is 16 at \(q=4,n=4\), but the universal pattern-sensitive fractional packing raises this to 19 and an explicit 19-word code reaches it. This is an exact solved finite q-ary instance plus a valid nontrivial lower bound for every alphabet, not an arbitrary slice or a claimed infinitely general exact formula. Detailed construction can seed improved finite covering bounds.
